SECTION 1 — MCQ (90 questions)

UNIT 1 — INTRODUCTION TO NETWORK

1.1. Basics of Network

MCQ 1
Question

What is the benefit of the Networking?

MCQUnit 11.1. Basics of Network ★

Options:

  1. A. File Sharing
  2. B. Easier access to Resources
  3. C. Easier Backups
  4. D. All of the Above

Correct Answer:

D — All of the Above

Explanation:

File sharing (A), easier access to resources (B) and easier backups (C) are all genuine advantages of networking, so the most complete choice is D — All of the Above.

  • File sharing: documents are stored once on a server/share and used by everyone.
  • Easier access to resources: printers, scanners, Internet connection and storage are shared.
  • Easier backups: central servers with RAID and scheduled backups protect data far better than individual PCs with pen drives.

Other advantages that could equally be listed: communication (e-mail/chat), centralised administration, cost saving and scalability.

MCQ 2
Question

A set of rules that govern all aspects of information communication is called

MCQUnit 11.1. Basics of Network ★

Options:

  1. A. Server
  2. B. Internet
  3. C. Protocol
  4. D. OSI Model

Correct Answer:

C — Protocol

Explanation:

A protocol is a set of rules that governs all aspects of information communication — message format, meaning of each field, order of messages, error handling and timing. C — Protocol is therefore correct.

  • A. Server is a computer that provides services; it is not a set of rules.
  • B. Internet is the global network of networks.
  • D. OSI model is a reference model that describes layers of communication; the model itself is not the set of rules used on the wire — the protocols are.
MCQ 3
Question

A set of a rule that governs data communication.

MCQUnit 11.1. Basics of Network ★

Options:

  1. A. Protocols
  2. B. Server
  3. C. Client
  4. D. Standards

Correct Answer:

A — Protocols

Explanation:

The sentence "a set of rules that governs data communication" is the definition of a protocol, so option A — Protocols is correct. (Questions 2 and 3 test the same concept with slightly different wording; the answer remains "protocol(s)".)

  • B. Server and C. Client are the two roles in a client–server application; neither defines rules.
  • D. Standards are the agreed documents (RFCs, IEEE 802.3) from which protocols are written — a related but different term. Example protocol: HTTP (rules for Web access), TCP (rules for reliable transport).
MCQ 4
Question

A ______ is a system in which multiple computers are connected to each other to share information and resources.

MCQUnit 11.1. Basics of Network ★

Options:

  1. A. Hardware
  2. B. Software
  3. C. Number System
  4. D. Computer Network

Correct Answer:

D — Computer Network

Explanation:

Two or more computers connected together so that they can share information and resources form a computer network — option D.

  • A. Hardware and B. Software are components of a network, not the network.
  • C. Number system is unrelated (it belongs to mathematics/computer fundamentals).

Example: the five PCs, one switch and one printer in a lab connected by UTP cable form a LAN — a computer network.

MCQ 5
Question

Two devices are in network if

MCQUnit 11.1. Basics of Network

Options:

  1. A. A process in one device is able to exchange information with a process in another device
  2. B. A process is running on both devices
  3. C. PIDs of the processes running of different devices are same
  4. D. A process is active and another is inactive

Correct Answer:

A — A process in one device is able to exchange information with a process in another device

Explanation:

Two devices are said to be "in a network" (interoperating) when a process running on one device can exchange information with a process running on the other. Hence A is correct.

  • B is not enough — processes may be running on both machines but not communicating.
  • C is wrong — process IDs (PIDs) are local to each machine and need not match at all.
  • D is wrong — both the sending and the receiving processes must be active to exchange information.

1.1.1. Types of Networks

MCQ 6
Question

Explain different types of network.

MCQUnit 11.1.1. Types of Networks ★★★

Answer:

Direct answer: networks are classified by geographical span and ownership into PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN (plus the specialised CAN, SAN, WLAN and VPN), each differing in range, speed, cost and error rate.

Definition: Networks are classified according to their geographical span, ownership and purpose. The standard classification is PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN (with CAN, SAN and WLAN as specialised forms).

1. PAN — Personal Area Network
  • Covers a very short distance, roughly 1–10 metres, around one person.
  • Technologies: Bluetooth, Infrared, ZigBee, USB, Wi-Fi Direct.
  • Example: mobile phone connected to a Bluetooth headset or smart-watch; laptop tethered to a phone.
  • Low cost, low power, low data rate; easy to set up but very limited range.
2. LAN — Local Area Network
  • Covers one room, building, school, office or campus (up to about 1–2 km).
  • Privately owned; uses UTP cable, coaxial cable, fibre or Wi-Fi; devices: hub, switch, router, NIC.
  • Speeds: 100 Mbps – 10 Gbps and more; very low error rate; high speed at low cost.
  • Topologies used: star (most common with switches) or bus (older).
  • Examples: computer laboratory network, office network, home Wi-Fi network.
3. MAN — Metropolitan Area Network
  • Covers a city or metropolitan area, roughly 5–50 km.
  • Usually owned by a single organisation or a service provider (telecom company, cable operator, city corporation).
  • Connects several LANs of different offices; technologies: Metro Ethernet, fibre rings, cable TV network, WiMAX.
  • Speeds: 10 Mbps – 10 Gbps; higher cost than LAN; medium error rate.
  • Examples: cable TV network of a city, network of all branches of a bank in one city, city-wide surveillance network.
4. WAN — Wide Area Network
  • Covers a country, continent or the whole world; range above 50 km, unlimited.
  • Not owned by one organisation; assembled from links leased from telecom carriers.
  • Technologies: leased lines, MPLS, VSAT, 4G/5G backhaul, submarine optical fibre; the Internet is the largest WAN.
  • Speeds vary from a few kbps to many Gbps; highest setup and running cost; error rate is highest because of long distance and many devices in the path.
  • Examples: the Internet, GTU-affiliated college network, network of a multinational company.
5. Other specialised types
  • CAN (Campus Area Network): several LANs inside one campus — between departments, library and hostels.
  • SAN (Storage Area Network): a dedicated high-speed network of storage devices (fibre channel, iSCSI) used by servers.
  • WLAN (Wireless LAN): LAN implemented with radio (IEEE 802.11 Wi-Fi) instead of cables.
  • VPN (Virtual Private Network): a private logical network created over a public network using encryption.
Comparison table
PointPANLANMANWAN
Range1–10 mUp to ~2 km5–50 km (city)Country / world
OwnershipIndividualPrivateSingle owner / providerMultiple organisations
SpeedLow (1–100 Mbps)Very high (100 Mbps–10 Gbps)High (10 Mbps–10 Gbps)Varies (kbps–Gbps)
Error rateLowLowestModerateHighest
CostVery lowLowModerateVery high
ExampleBluetooth headsetComputer labCable TV / city bank networkInternet, MNC network

Conclusion: the type of network is chosen by the distance to be covered and the purpose to be served — PAN for a person, LAN for a building, MAN for a city and WAN for a country or the world — with CAN, SAN, WLAN and VPN as specialised forms of the same idea.

  • CAN (Campus Area Network): several LANs inside one campus — between departments, library and hostels.
  • SAN (Storage Area Network): a dedicated high-speed network of storage devices (fibre channel, iSCSI) used by servers.
  • WLAN (Wireless LAN): LAN implemented with radio (IEEE 802.11 Wi-Fi) instead of cables.
  • VPN (Virtual Private Network): a private logical network created over a public network using encryption.
Comparison table
PointPANLANMANWAN
Range1–10 mUp to ~2 km5–50 km (city)Country / world
OwnershipIndividualPrivateSingle owner / providerMultiple organisations
SpeedLow (1–100 Mbps)Very high (100 Mbps–10 Gbps)High (10 Mbps–10 Gbps)Varies (kbps–Gbps)
Error rateLowLowestModerateHighest
CostVery lowLowModerateVery high
ExampleBluetooth headsetComputer labCable TV / city bank networkInternet, MNC network

Conclusion: a network is classified as PAN, LAN, MAN or WAN according to its span, speed, ownership and cost; the smaller the span the faster and cheaper the technology, and a single organisation normally operates several of these types together.

MCQ 8
Question

Explain different types of Networks.

MCQUnit 11.1.1. Types of Networks ★

Answer:

Direct answer: the different types of networks, classified by their geographical span, are PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN; specialised networks include CAN, SAN, WLAN and VPN.

Definition: Networks are classified according to their geographical span, ownership and purpose. The standard classification is PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN (with CAN, SAN and WLAN as specialised forms).

1. PAN — Personal Area Network
  • Covers a very short distance, roughly 1–10 metres, around one person.
  • Technologies: Bluetooth, Infrared, ZigBee, USB, Wi-Fi Direct.
  • Example: mobile phone connected to a Bluetooth headset or smart-watch; laptop tethered to a phone.
  • Low cost, low power, low data rate; easy to set up but very limited range.
2. LAN — Local Area Network
  • Covers one room, building, school, office or campus (up to about 1–2 km).
  • Privately owned; uses UTP cable, coaxial cable, fibre or Wi-Fi; devices: hub, switch, router, NIC.
  • Speeds: 100 Mbps – 10 Gbps and more; very low error rate; high speed at low cost.
  • Topologies used: star (most common with switches) or bus (older).
  • Examples: computer laboratory network, office network, home Wi-Fi network.
3. MAN — Metropolitan Area Network
  • Covers a city or metropolitan area, roughly 5–50 km.
  • Usually owned by a single organisation or a service provider (telecom company, cable operator, city corporation).
  • Connects several LANs of different offices; technologies: Metro Ethernet, fibre rings, cable TV network, WiMAX.
  • Speeds: 10 Mbps – 10 Gbps; higher cost than LAN; medium error rate.
  • Examples: cable TV network of a city, network of all branches of a bank in one city, city-wide surveillance network.
4. WAN — Wide Area Network
  • Covers a country, continent or the whole world; range above 50 km, unlimited.
  • Not owned by one organisation; assembled from links leased from telecom carriers.
  • Technologies: leased lines, MPLS, VSAT, 4G/5G backhaul, submarine optical fibre; the Internet is the largest WAN.
  • Speeds vary from a few kbps to many Gbps; highest setup and running cost; error rate is highest because of long distance and many devices in the path.
  • Examples: the Internet, GTU-affiliated college network, network of a multinational company.
5. Other specialised types
  • CAN (Campus Area Network): several LANs inside one campus — between departments, library and hostels.
  • SAN (Storage Area Network): a dedicated high-speed network of storage devices (fibre channel, iSCSI) used by servers.
  • WLAN (Wireless LAN): LAN implemented with radio (IEEE 802.11 Wi-Fi) instead of cables.
  • VPN (Virtual Private Network): a private logical network created over a public network using encryption.
Comparison table
PointPANLANMANWAN
Range1–10 mUp to ~2 km5–50 km (city)Country / world
OwnershipIndividualPrivateSingle owner / providerMultiple organisations
SpeedLow (1–100 Mbps)Very high (100 Mbps–10 Gbps)High (10 Mbps–10 Gbps)Varies (kbps–Gbps)
Error rateLowLowestModerateHighest
CostVery lowLowModerateVery high
ExampleBluetooth headsetComputer labCable TV / city bank networkInternet, MNC network

Conclusion: the different types of networks — PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN and their specialised forms — differ in range, bandwidth, ownership and error rate, and selecting the right type for each requirement keeps the network economical and efficient.

MCQ 9
Question

What is Network? Explain advantages and disadvantages of Networks.

MCQUnit 11.1.1. Types of Networks ★★★

Answer:

Direct answer: a network connects two or more autonomous computers for sharing data and resources; its definition, advantages and disadvantages are given below with comparison tables.

Definition: A computer network is a collection of two or more autonomous computers (and other devices such as printers, switches and servers) interconnected by a transmission medium — guided (cable) or unguided (wireless) — and following a common set of rules called protocols, so that they can exchange data and share hardware, software and information resources.

Each device in the network (called a node or host) can both send and receive data; no node is the master of another node — this is why the term autonomous is used in the definition. Data travels over the network in small units such as frames, packets and segments.

Advantages of networking
AdvantageExplanation
Resource sharingOne printer, scanner, plotter or disk array can be used by all users, saving money and space.
File and data sharingFiles can be copied and accessed across machines quickly instead of using pen drives or e-mail.
CommunicationE-mail, chat, video conferencing, VoIP and social applications depend completely on networks.
Centralised managementSoftware installation, user accounts, antivirus updates and policies are managed from a server for all clients.
Easier backup and reliabilityData is stored on servers with RAID and scheduled backups; a failed PC does not destroy the data.
Cost effectivenessShared Internet connection, shared licensed software and distributed processing reduce per-user cost.
Scalability and remote accessNew nodes and new sites can be added easily; users can work from home or branch offices (VPN, cloud).
Disadvantages of networking
DisadvantageExplanation
High initial costCabling, switches, servers, licences and skilled manpower are required.
Security threatsViruses, worms, ransomware, hacking, phishing and data leakage become possible.
Administration and maintenanceA network administrator, monitoring tools and periodic maintenance are essential.
Single point of failureIf the server or central switch fails, the whole network (or a large part of it) may stop working.
Performance dependenceSpeed falls when traffic increases; congestion, collisions and latency degrade service.
Privacy concernsEmployee activity can be monitored; personal data moves over shared media and may be intercepted.
Virus propagationMalware spreads from one machine to many in seconds.
Conclusion: Networking multiplies the usefulness of a computer many times over by sharing resources and enabling communication; the cost is money, administration effort and security risk, which are controlled by proper design, firewalls, antivirus and trained staff.

Conclusion: a network links autonomous computers so that they can exchange data and share resources; its advantages (sharing, communication, central management, backups, low cost) are weighed against its disadvantages (cost, security, administration, single point of failure, performance dependence), which are controlled by good design.

1.1.2. Different Topologies

MCQ 10
Question

Which network topology requires HUB or central controller device?

MCQUnit 11.1.2. Different Topologies ★★★

Options:

  1. A. Bus
  2. B. Ring
  3. C. Star
  4. D. Mesh

Correct Answer:

C — Star

Explanation:

In a star topology every node has a separate point-to-point link to a central device — a hub (layer 1) or a switch (layer 2). The question says "HUB or central controller device", so C — Star is correct. (Question 12 asks the same thing with the wording "central controller or hub" and the option order changed; the answer there is "star" again.)

  • A. Bus — one backbone cable, no central device.
  • B. Ring — nodes form a closed loop; access is controlled by a token, not a hub.
  • D. Mesh — every node is connected to every other node; no centre.
MCQ 11
Question

Physical or logical arrangement of network is

MCQUnit 11.1.2. Different Topologies ★

Options:

  1. A. topology
  2. B. routing
  3. C. networking
  4. D. control

Correct Answer:

A — topology

Explanation:

The physical or logical arrangement of network nodes and links is called the network topology — option A. Typical topologies: bus, star, ring, mesh, tree and hybrid.

  • B. Routing is the process of selecting a path for packets at layer 3.
  • C. Networking is the general activity of connecting computers.
  • D. Control refers to flow/error/access control mechanisms, not layout.
MCQ 12
Question

Which network topology requires a central controler or hub?

MCQUnit 11.1.2. Different Topologies ★

Options:

  1. A. star
  2. B. mesh
  3. C. ring
  4. D. bus

Correct Answer:

A — star

Explanation:

Repetition of MCQ 10 with shuffled options: a network that needs a central controller (hub or switch) is a star topology, hence A — star.

Remember the shape: all nodes radiate from one central device like a star; a switch in a modern LAN is exactly this central device, and disconnecting one cable affects only that one node.

MCQ 13
Question

A topology that involves Tokens.

MCQUnit 11.1.2. Different Topologies ★

Options:

  1. A. Star
  2. B. Bus
  3. C. Ring
  4. D. Mesh

Correct Answer:

C — Ring

Explanation:

Ring topology uses a special frame called a token: only the node holding the token may transmit, which guarantees collision-free, deterministic access. So C — Ring is correct (used by Token Ring and FDDI networks).

  • A. Star uses a central hub/switch and contention (CSMA/CD) or switching.
  • B. Bus uses CSMA/CD with a shared backbone.
  • D. Mesh uses dedicated links and no access-control token.
MCQ 14
Question

Ethernet system uses which of the following technology.

MCQUnit 11.1.2. Different Topologies ★

Options:

  1. A. Bus
  2. B. Ring
  3. C. Star
  4. D. Tree

Correct Answer:

A — Bus

Explanation:

Classical Ethernet (10Base5 "thicknet" and 10Base2 "thinnet") was based on the bus topology: all stations tapped one coaxial backbone and shared it using CSMA/CD, so A — Bus is the expected answer.

Ambiguity note (important for exams): modern switched Ethernet is physically a star (each PC to a switch) while its logical behaviour is a "switched bus" inside the switch. If a paper says "Ethernet uses which topology?", the traditional answer expected is bus; if it says "today's Ethernet LAN", the physical answer is star.
MCQ 15
Question

If you see a group of networked computers connected to a central hub, you know that the network has what type of physical topology?

MCQUnit 11.1.2. Different Topologies ★

Options:

  1. A. Ring
  2. B. Star
  3. C. Bus
  4. D. Cannot tell

Correct Answer:

B — Star

Explanation:

A group of computers cabled to one central hub is the definition of a star physical topology — option B.

  • A. Ring would require each PC to be linked to the next one in a closed loop.
  • C. Bus would require a single backbone with taps, not a hub.
  • D. "Cannot tell" is wrong here because the physical layout is directly visible.
MCQ 16
Question

Which type of topology is best suited for large businesses which must carefully control and coordinate the operation of distributed branch outlets?

MCQUnit 11.1.2. Different Topologies ★

Options:

  1. A. Ring
  2. B. Star
  3. C. Bus
  4. D. Tree

Correct Answer:

D — Tree

Explanation:

Large businesses with distributed branch outlets need a hierarchy of networks that can be expanded branch by branch — that is the tree (hierarchical) topology, option D. A tree is built from groups of star networks joined to a backbone, so it is easy to manage department-wise and to extend to new branches.

  • A. Ring / B. Star / C. Bus are single-segment layouts that do not scale to a hierarchy of branches; a star covers only one office building, and a bus only one segment.
MCQ 17
Question

Communication channel is shared by all the machines on the network in

MCQUnit 11.1.2. Different Topologies ★★★

Options:

  1. A. Broadcast network
  2. B. Unicast network
  3. C. Multicast network
  4. D. Anycast network

Correct Answer:

A — Broadcast network

Explanation:

When one communication channel is shared by all machines on the network (as in a bus LAN or Ethernet), the network is called a broadcast network — every transmitted frame reaches every station and the addressed station accepts it; A is correct.

  • B. Unicast network means one-to-one delivery.
  • C. Multicast network means one-to-many delivery to a group, not to all machines.
  • D. Anycast network means delivery to the nearest member of a group.
MCQ 18
Question

What is Multicast?

MCQUnit 11.1.2. Different Topologies ★★

Options:

  1. A. sending the data from one source to so many receivers
  2. B. sending the data from one source to one receiver
  3. C. sending the data from one source to all receivers
  4. D. None of these

Correct Answer:

A — sending the data from one source to so many receivers

Explanation:

Multicast = one source sending to a group of receivers that have joined a multicast group, i.e. "one source to many (but not all) receivers" — option A.

  • B describes unicast (one-to-one).
  • C describes broadcast (one-to-all).
  • D "None of these" is wrong because A fits.

Example: live lecture streaming to 5,000 students uses multicast address range 224.0.0.0–239.255.255.255 (Class D).

1.2. Types of Networks (LAN, MAN, WAN)

MCQ 19
Question

The term WAN stands for?

MCQUnit 11.2. Types of Networks (LAN, MAN, WAN) ★★

Options:

  1. A. Wide Area Net
  2. B. Wide Access Net
  3. C. Wide Area Network
  4. D. Wide Access Network

Correct Answer:

C — Wide Area Network

Explanation:

WAN = Wide Area Network — a network that spans a large geographical area such as a city, country or the whole world (the Internet is the largest WAN). Hence option C.

Options A ("Wide Area Net") and B/D ("Wide Access Network") are distractors based on wrong expansions. Comparison: LAN (building, high speed), MAN (city), WAN (country/world, usually owned by carriers).

MCQ 20
Question

What is Internet?

MCQUnit 11.2. Types of Networks (LAN, MAN, WAN) ★★

Options:

  1. A. A single network
  2. B. A vast collection of different networks
  3. C. Interconnection of local area networks
  4. D. Interconnection of wide area networks

Correct Answer:

B — A vast collection of different networks

Explanation:

The Internet is not a single network but a vast collection of different networks interconnected by routers and speaking the common TCP/IP protocol suite — option B.

  • A is wrong — no single network covers the world.
  • C and D are partially true but incomplete: the Internet interconnects LANs, MANs and WANs alike; it is not only a set of local or wide area networks that are interconnected in one uniform way.

1.3. Terminologies

MCQ 21
Question

What is Internet?

MCQUnit 11.3. Terminologies ★

Options:

  1. A. Combination of LANS
  2. B. Group of unrelated computers
  3. C. Group of WANS
  4. D. An Internal Network

Correct Answer:

A — Combination of LANS

Explanation:

The Internet is formed by interconnecting many individual networks (LANs/MANs/WANs of companies, universities and ISPs) into one global network; among the given choices, A — Combination of LANs is the expected answer.

Ambiguity note: purely technically, the Internet is a "network of networks" — LANs joined through WAN links and ISPs — so option C (Group of WANs) is only partly right and would ignore the LANs. Answer keys normally accept option A. Option D ("An Internal Network") describes an intranet, not the Internet.
MCQ 22
Question

What is the term for a private network used within an organization?

MCQUnit 11.3. Terminologies ★

Options:

  1. A. Internet
  2. B. Intranet
  3. C. Extranet
  4. D. Broadcast

Correct Answer:

B — Intranet

Explanation:

A private network used inside one organisation is an intranet — option B. It uses Internet technologies (TCP/IP, Web server, browser) but is protected by a firewall and is accessible only to employees.

  • A. Internet — public worldwide network.
  • C. Extranet — an intranet extended to trusted outsiders (partners, suppliers) with authentication.
  • D. Broadcast — a transmission type, not a network type.
MCQ 23
Question

Which of the following protocols is used in the internet?

MCQUnit 11.3. Terminologies ★

Options:

  1. A. HTTP
  2. B. DHCP
  3. C. DNS
  4. D. DNS, HTTP

Correct Answer:

D — DNS, HTTP

Explanation:

The Internet uses many application-layer protocols; HTTP (Web), DHCP (automatic IP configuration) and DNS (name resolution) are all used. Since option D lists DNS, HTTP together, it is the most complete answer among the choices, so D is selected.

  • A (HTTP only) and C (DNS only) are each individually true but incomplete.
  • B (DHCP only) is likewise incomplete — DHCP is essential for automatic addressing but is not the only protocol used.
Exam tip: when two individually-correct options are given and one option combines them, the combined option is the expected answer.

UNIT 2 — INTERNET AND INTRANET

2.1. Concepts of Internet and Intranet

MCQ 24
Question

Which of the following is the functionality of network layer?

MCQUnit 22.1. Concepts of Internet and Intranet

Options:

  1. A. Synchronization of bits
  2. B. Dialog control
  3. C. Compression
  4. D. Logical addressing

Correct Answer:

D — Logical addressing

Explanation:

The network layer (layer 3) is responsible for logical addressing (IP addresses) and routing packets between different networks — so option D is correct.

  • A. Synchronisation of bits — physical layer (layer 1).
  • B. Dialog control — session layer (layer 5): deciding whose turn it is to transmit.
  • C. Compression — presentation layer (layer 6), along with translation and encryption.
MCQ 25
Question

The ______ model supports both connectionless and connection oriented communication in the network layer.

MCQUnit 22.1. Concepts of Internet and Intranet

Options:

  1. A. TCP/IP
  2. B. OSI
  3. C. Both
  4. D. None

Correct Answer:

A — TCP/IP

Explanation:

The TCP/IP model supports both connectionless and connection-oriented operation at its Internet (network) layer — IP itself is connectionless, while TCP provides connection-oriented service at the transport layer above it; the reference papers therefore mark A — TCP/IP.

  • B. OSI describes the two services in theory (CLNS/CONS) but the question's expected answer follows the working protocol suite, TCP/IP.
  • C "Both" and D "None" are distractors for this option set.
Concept to write in the exam: IP = connectionless datagram service; TCP = connection-oriented reliable service; UDP = connectionless unreliable service. Together they give the TCP/IP suite both types of communication.

2.1.1. Working of Internet and its Architecture

MCQ 26
Question

A NFS allows a computer to access and use files over a network. What does the acronym NFS stand for?

MCQUnit 22.1.1. Working of Internet and its Architecture ★

Options:

  1. A. network file system
  2. B. network file search
  3. C. new file system
  4. D. new file search

Correct Answer:

A — network file system

Explanation:

NFS = Network File System — a client/server file system protocol (developed by Sun Microsystems, standardised in RFC 1094/1813) that lets a computer mount and use files and directories stored on another computer over the network as if they were local. Hence A.

Options B, C and D are invented expansions ("network file search", "new file system", "new file search") and are wrong.

2.1.2. Working of Intranet and its Architecture

MCQ 27
Question

A ______ allows a computer to access and use files over a network.

MCQUnit 22.1.2. Working of Intranet and its Architecture ★

Options:

  1. A. Network file system
  2. B. Network file search
  3. C. New file system
  4. D. New file search

Correct Answer:

A — Network file system

Explanation:

The same concept as MCQ 26, in fill-in-the-blank form: a Network file system allows a computer to access and use files over a network, so A is correct. On Linux/Unix the NFS server exports a directory (/etc/exports) and the client mounts it with mount -t nfs server:/share /mnt.

2.1.3. Network Devices

MCQ 28
Question

Which one of the following network devices work in the data link layer?

MCQUnit 22.1.3. Network Devices ★★

Options:

  1. A. Router
  2. B. Switch
  3. C. Both A and B
  4. D. None of the above

Correct Answer:

B — Switch

Explanation:

Among the given devices only the switch works at the data link layer (layer 2) — it forwards frames using MAC addresses, so option B is correct.

  • A. Router works at layer 3 (network layer) using IP addresses.
  • C. Both A and B would wrongly include the router.
  • D is wrong because the switch does work at layer 2.
MCQ 29
Question

Which network device operates at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2) of the OSI model?

MCQUnit 22.1.3. Network Devices ★

Options:

  1. A. Router
  2. B. Hub
  3. C. Firewall
  4. D. Switch

Correct Answer:

D — Switch

Explanation:

The device that operates at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2) is the switch — option D. A switch learns source MAC addresses, builds a MAC address table and forwards frames only to the port where the destination MAC is reachable; it also breaks the network into one collision domain per port.

  • A. Router — layer 3; B. Hub — layer 1 (repeats everything out of all ports).
  • C. Firewall — works on layers 3–7 depending on type.
MCQ 30
Question

Which one of the following network devices works in half-duplex?

MCQUnit 22.1.3. Network Devices

Options:

  1. A. Router
  2. B. Switch
  3. C. Hub
  4. D. None of the above

Correct Answer:

C — Hub

Explanation:

A hub works in half-duplex: all ports share one collision domain and only one station can transmit at a time (CSMA/CD), so C is correct.

  • A. Router and B. Switch use full-duplex links (a switch port can send and receive simultaneously).
  • D is wrong because the hub is explicitly listed as option C.
MCQ 31
Question

Which of the following devices does not require power to forward the signals?

MCQUnit 22.1.3. Network Devices ★

Options:

  1. A. Active Hub
  2. B. Passive Hub
  3. C. Repeater
  4. D. Bridge

Correct Answer:

B — Passive Hub

Explanation:

A passive hub does not regenerate or amplify signals — it merely provides the electrical connection between cables, so it needs no power supply. Hence B.

  • A. Active hub needs power because it regenerates and amplifies the signal.
  • C. Repeater and D. Bridge are both powered devices (a repeater amplifies the signal; a bridge stores frames and inspects MAC addresses, so it needs logic and power).
MCQ 32
Question

Which one of the following network devices is the multicast device?

MCQUnit 22.1.3. Network Devices

Options:

  1. A. Router
  2. B. Switch
  3. C. Both A and B
  4. D. None of the above

Correct Answer:

A — Router

Explanation:

Among the options, the router is the multicast-capable device: it runs IGMP and multicast routing protocols (PIM, DVMRP) and forwards packets to multicast group addresses (224.0.0.0–239.255.255.255). Hence the expected answer is A.

Ambiguity note: a layer-2 switch also handles multicast efficiently in a switched LAN using IGMP snooping (it forwards group traffic only to interested ports) — which is why some modern answer keys might prefer "Both A and B". The classical examination answer for this question is Router, because routing multicast between networks is a layer-3 job.
MCQ 33
Question

Which one of the following has MAC address and IP address?

MCQUnit 22.1.3. Network Devices

Options:

  1. A. Router
  2. B. Repeater
  3. C. Hub
  4. D. Modem

Correct Answer:

A — Router

Explanation:

A router has both physical (MAC) addresses on its interfaces and logical (IP) addresses that it uses to route packets between networks — hence option A.

  • B. Repeater and C. Hub are layer-1 devices: they have no MAC or IP address.
  • D. Modem converts signals; a simple modem has neither address, although modern cable/DSL modem-routers do — since the question expects one device, the router is the intended answer.

2.2. Types of Cables

MCQ 34
Question

Which cables are used to connect computers?

MCQUnit 22.2. Types of Cables ★

Options:

  1. A. Twisted Pair
  2. B. Ethernet Cable
  3. C. Coaxial
  4. D. Fiber

Correct Answer:

A — Twisted Pair

Explanation:

Among the listed cable types, Twisted Pair (UTP with RJ45) is the standard cable used to connect computers in a LAN; it is the cheapest and most widely installed — option A is the expected answer.

Ambiguity note: coaxial and fibre cable also connect computers in specific situations, and "Ethernet cable" is a general name (usually meaning UTP). Since the question wants the ordinary LAN cabling, the key answer is Twisted Pair. Fibre has the highest bandwidth but is used for backbones, not ordinary desktop connections.
MCQ 35
Question

Which type of cable uses RJ45 connector?

MCQUnit 22.2. Types of Cables ★

Options:

  1. A. Fiber Optic cable
  2. B. Co-axial Cable
  3. C. Telephone Cable
  4. D. Unshielded Twisted Pair Cable

Correct Answer:

D — Unshielded Twisted Pair Cable

Explanation:

The RJ45 (8P8C) connector is used with Unshielded Twisted Pair cable — option D. UTP LAN cable uses 8 wires in 4 twisted pairs, and the RJ45 plug has 8 contacts.

  • A. Fibre optic uses ST/SC/LC connectors, B. coaxial uses BNC/F connectors, and C. telephone cable uses the smaller RJ11 (6 contacts).
MCQ 36
Question

Which of following cable types offers highest bandwidth and speed?

MCQUnit 22.2. Types of Cables

Options:

  1. A. UTP
  2. B. Coaxial
  3. C. Fiber Optic
  4. D. HDMI

Correct Answer:

C — Fiber Optic

Explanation:

Fibre optic cable carries data as light and offers the highest bandwidth and speed over the longest distance with total immunity to electromagnetic interference — option C.

  • A. UTP — cheap, 100 m limit, up to 10 Gbps in high categories.
  • B. Coaxial — better than UTP but far below fibre.
  • D. HDMI is a consumer audio–video interface at most a few metres, not a network backbone medium.
MCQ 37
Question

The ____ carry signal in light form.

MCQUnit 22.2. Types of Cables ★

Options:

  1. A. Twisted air cable
  2. B. Coaxial cable
  3. C. Fiber optics
  4. D. None of above

Correct Answer:

C — Fiber optics

Explanation:

Fibre optics carry the signal in the form of light pulses, guided by total internal reflection inside a glass core — option C.

  • A. "Twisted air cable" is not a real cable type.
  • B. Coaxial cable carries electrical (voltage/current) signals, not light.
  • D is wrong because fibre genuinely carries light.
MCQ 38
Question

Fiber optics posses following properties

MCQUnit 22.2. Types of Cables

Options:

  1. A. Immune electromagnetic interference
  2. B. Very less signal attenuation
  3. C. Very hard to tap
  4. D. All of the mentioned

Correct Answer:

D — All of the mentioned

Explanation:

All three properties are true of fibre optics: it is immune to electromagnetic interference, has very low signal attenuation (very long distances without repeaters) and is very hard to tap (tapping emits light loss that is easy to detect, so it is secure). Therefore D — All of the mentioned.

MCQ 39
Question

What kind of transmission medium is most appropriate to carry data in a computer network that is exposed to electrical interferences?

MCQUnit 22.2. Types of Cables ★

Options:

  1. A. Optical fiber
  2. B. Fiber optics
  3. C. Coaxial cable
  4. D. Unshielded twisted pair

Correct Answer:

A — Optical fiber

Explanation:

Where electrical interference is present, an optical fibre link is the right choice because it carries light, not electricity, so motors, fluorescent lamps, radio transmitters and lightning cannot disturb it — option A is correct.

Ambiguity note: options A ("Optical fiber") and B ("Fiber optics") refer to the same medium; the precise technical term asked in the original key is optical fiber. Option D (UTP) is the worst choice here because it picks up interference; coaxial is better but not immune.
MCQ 40
Question

Coaxial cable consists of concentric copper conductors.

MCQUnit 22.2. Types of Cables

Options:

  1. A. 1
  2. B. 2
  3. C. 3
  4. D. 4

Correct Answer:

B — 2

Explanation:

A coaxial cable has two concentric copper conductors — the inner centre conductor and the outer braided shield, separated by a dielectric and covered by a jacket — so option B (2) is correct.

Structure from inside out: centre conductor → dielectric insulator → braided shield → protective jacket. The shield's concentric geometry is what gives the cable its name and its good noise immunity.

UNIT 3 — MOBILE AD HOC NETWORK

3.1. Concepts and Types of MANET

MCQ 41
Question

What does MANET stand for?

MCQUnit 33.1. Concepts and Types of MANET ★★

Options:

  1. A. My Access Network
  2. B. Mobile Ad hoc Network
  3. C. Modem Access Network
  4. D. Media Ad hoc Network

Correct Answer:

B — Mobile Ad hoc Network

Explanation:

MANET = Mobile Ad hoc Network — an infrastructure-less, self-configuring wireless network of mobile nodes that forward each other's packets (multi-hop). Hence B.

The other expansions ("My Access Network", "Modem Access Network", "Media Ad hoc Network") are invented distractors. Key facts for the exam: no access point, dynamic topology, every node acts as a router, routing protocols AODV/DSR/OLSR.

MCQ 42
Question

What does FANET stand for?

MCQUnit 33.1. Concepts and Types of MANET ★

Options:

  1. A. Fixed Area Network
  2. B. Fiber Ad hoc Network
  3. C. Flying Ad hoc Network
  4. D. Fast Access Network

Correct Answer:

C — Flying Ad hoc Network

Explanation:

FANET = Flying Ad hoc Network — an ad hoc network whose nodes are unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs/drones) that communicate with each other and with ground stations. Hence C.

FANETs share the MANET principle but add three-dimensional mobility, longer radio ranges and line-of-sight constraints; applications include surveillance, disaster mapping, delivery and agriculture.

MCQ 43
Question

What does VANET stand for?

MCQUnit 33.1. Concepts and Types of MANET ★★

Options:

  1. A. Vehicular AdHoc Network
  2. B. Vehicular Address Network
  3. C. Vehicular Adhoc Neural Network
  4. D. Wireless Sensor Networks

Correct Answer:

A — Vehicular AdHoc Network

Explanation:

VANET = Vehicular Ad hoc Network — an ad hoc network of vehicles fitted with on-board units, plus roadside units, used for safety and traffic applications (V2V, V2I communication). Hence A.

  • B "Vehicular Address Network" and C "Vehicular Adhoc Neural Network" are wrong expansions; D "Wireless Sensor Networks" is a different (related) network type.
MCQ 44
Question

Expansion of VANET is

MCQUnit 33.1. Concepts and Types of MANET

Options:

  1. A. Vehicular AdHoc Network
  2. B. Vehicular Address Network
  3. C. Vehicular AdHock Neural Network
  4. D. Vehicle Address Network

Correct Answer:

A — Vehicular AdHoc Network

Explanation:

Same concept with shuffled options: VANET expands to Vehicular Ad hoc Network — option A (also written "Vehicular AdHoc Network"). The spelling in options C and D is incorrect.

MCQ 45
Question

Full form of SPANC?

MCQUnit 33.1. Concepts and Types of MANET ★

Options:

  1. A. Smart phone Authorise Network
  2. B. Secure phone Ad hoc
  3. C. Smart people Ad hoc Network
  4. D. Smart phone Ad-hoc Network

Correct Answer:

D — Smart phone Ad-hoc Network

Explanation:

SPANC/SPANET refers to a Smart phone Ad-hoc Network — a network formed by smart phones using Bluetooth/Wi-Fi Direct without any operator infrastructure. The closest correct option is D — Smart phone Ad-hoc Network.

Terminology note: the standard expansion in the literature is SPANET = Smart Phone Ad hoc Network; the question paper writes "SPANC". Option C ("Smart people Ad hoc Network") is a distractor; A and B are invented.
MCQ 46
Question

Full form of SPANC.

MCQUnit 33.1. Concepts and Types of MANET

Options:

  1. A. smart plan adhoe network
  2. B. spaceplan adhoc network
  3. C. smartphone adhoc network
  4. D. spacious provide adhoc network

Correct Answer:

C — smartphone adhoc network

Explanation:

Same concept as MCQ 45 with lowercase options: the correct expansion is smartphone adhoc network — option C.

Remember: SPANET is used when a group of phone users creates a peer-to-peer network for chat, file sharing or emergency messages when no cellular network is available (disaster, crowded events, network shutdown).

3.2. Concepts of OSI Layers

MCQ 47
Question

OSI stands for ________.

MCQUnit 33.2. Concepts of OSI Layers ★★★

Options:

  1. A. Open system interconnection
  2. B. Operating system interface
  3. C. Optical service implementation
  4. D. Open service Internet

Correct Answer:

A — Open system interconnection

Explanation:

OSI = Open Systems Interconnection — the seven-layer reference model published by ISO in 1984 that standardises how open (non-proprietary) systems communicate. Hence A.

  • B "Operating system interface" — OSI is not about OS interfaces.
  • C "Optical service implementation" and D "Open service Internet" are invented distractors. Note that "open" in OSI means the standard is publicly defined, so any vendor can implement it.
MCQ 48
Question

The number of layers in OSI model is

MCQUnit 33.2. Concepts of OSI Layers

Options:

  1. A. 4
  2. B. 5
  3. C. 6
  4. D. 7

Correct Answer:

D — 7

Explanation:

The OSI model has seven layers — option D. From top to bottom: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data link, Physical (mnemonic: All People Seem To Need Data Processing).

Compare: the TCP/IP model has four layers (Application, Transport, Internet, Network access), and the five-layer teaching model merges the OSI application/presentation/session into one application layer.

MCQ 49
Question

Which layer is used to link the network support layers and user support layers?

MCQUnit 33.2. Concepts of OSI Layers ★★

Options:

  1. A. Session Layer
  2. B. Data Link Layer
  3. C. Transport Layer
  4. D. Network Layer

Correct Answer:

C — Transport Layer

Explanation:

The transport layer is the bridge between the network support layers (physical, data link, network) and the user support layers (session, presentation, application) — option C.

  • A. Session and layers above it serve the user, not the link between the two groups. B. Data link and D. Network belong to the lower (network support) group.
MCQ 50
Question

Which layer provides the services to user?

MCQUnit 33.2. Concepts of OSI Layers ★★

Options:

  1. A. Application layer
  2. B. Session layer
  3. C. Physical layer
  4. D. Transport layer

Correct Answer:

A — Application layer

Explanation:

The application layer provides services directly to the user's applications (HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS, Telnet) — option A.

  • B. Session layer organises the dialog between applications but does not provide the user-facing services.
  • C. Physical layer transmits bits; D. Transport layer delivers data between processes. Both are invisible to the user.
MCQ 51
Question

Which layer is responsible for process-to-process delivery?

MCQUnit 33.2. Concepts of OSI Layers ★★

Options:

  1. A. Physical layer
  2. B. Network layer
  3. C. Transport layer
  4. D. Application layer

Correct Answer:

C — Transport layer

Explanation:

The transport layer is responsible for process-to-process delivery: it uses port numbers to hand data to the correct application process on the destination host (TCP/UDP). Hence C.

  • A. Physical — bit-by-bit transmission; B. Network — host-to-host delivery across networks (logical addressing/routing); D. Application — the services themselves.
MCQ 52
Question

Which layer in the OSI model provides the data transfer in the form of frames across the Transmission link?

MCQUnit 33.2. Concepts of OSI Layers ★

Options:

  1. A. physical layer
  2. B. data link layer
  3. C. network layer
  4. D. application layer

Correct Answer:

B — data link layer

Explanation:

Data is transferred as frames at the data link layer, which adds MAC addresses and a CRC trailer to the packet — option B.

PDU at each layer: application — message; transport — segment (TCP) / datagram (UDP); network — packet/datagram; data link — frame; physical — bits. The word "frames" in the question is the direct clue.

MCQ 53
Question

The design issue of Datalink Layer in OSI Reference Model is

MCQUnit 33.2. Concepts of OSI Layers

Options:

  1. A. Framing
  2. B. Representation of bits
  3. C. Synchronization of bits
  4. D. Connection control

Correct Answer:

A — Framing

Explanation:

The classical design issue of the data link layer is framing: the layer must mark the beginning and end of each frame so the receiver can identify it on a continuous bit stream — option A.

  • B. Representation of bits and C. Synchronisation of bits are physical-layer issues. D. Connection control is a data link/service function but "framing" is the textbook's headline design issue, and it is what the original key expects.
MCQ 54
Question

The physical layer is responsible for

MCQUnit 33.2. Concepts of OSI Layers ★★

Options:

  1. A. Line coding
  2. B. Channel coding
  3. C. Modulation
  4. D. All of the above

Correct Answer:

D — All of the above

Explanation:

The physical layer handles line coding (converting bits to a signal), channel coding (adding redundancy for error handling) and modulation (varying a carrier: ASK, FSK, PSK, QAM) — so D — All of the above is correct.

It also defines data rate, bit synchronisation, transmission mode, topology and the mechanical/ electrical specifications of cables and connectors.

MCQ 55
Question

The physical layer provides

MCQUnit 33.2. Concepts of OSI Layers ★

Options:

  1. A. Mechanical specifications of electrical connectors and cables
  2. B. Electrical specification of transmission line signal level
  3. C. Specification for IR over optical fiber
  4. D. All of the mentioned

Correct Answer:

D — All of the mentioned

Explanation:

The physical layer specifies the mechanical details of connectors and cables, the electrical signal levels of the transmission line and the specifications for optical transmission over fibre (among many other things) — hence D — All of the mentioned.

Remember that the physical layer deals with bits and signals only; it has no idea of frames, packets or addresses.

MCQ 56
Question

The functionalities of the presentation layer include

MCQUnit 33.2. Concepts of OSI Layers ★★

Options:

  1. A. Data compression
  2. B. Data encryption
  3. C. Data description
  4. D. All of the above

Correct Answer:

D — All of the above

Explanation:

The presentation layer performs translation (data description/format conversion), encryption and compression — all three options are its functions, so D — All of the above.

Examples: ASCII ↔ EBCDIC ↔ Unicode conversion, SSL/TLS encryption, JPEG/MPEG compression, MIME encoding of mail attachments.

MCQ 57
Question

Which of the following layers does the HTTP protocol work on?

MCQUnit 33.2. Concepts of OSI Layers ★

Options:

  1. A. Physical layer
  2. B. Data link layer
  3. C. Application layer
  4. D. None of these

Correct Answer:

C — Application layer

Explanation:

HTTP is an application layer protocol (layer 7) — option C. It defines the request–response rules used by Web browsers and Web servers and normally uses TCP port 80 (HTTPS uses port 443 with TLS).

  • Physical and data link layers move bits and frames; they never see HTTP messages.
  • Note: HTTPS = HTTP running over TLS, but HTTP itself is still classified at the application layer.
MCQ 58
Question

Application layer is implemented in

MCQUnit 33.2. Concepts of OSI Layers

Options:

  1. A. End system by NIC
  2. B. NIC
  3. C. Ethernet
  4. D. Packet transport

Correct Answer:

A — End system by NIC

Explanation:

The application layer is implemented in the end system (host) as software — the Web browser, mail client or server program — not inside the NIC. Among the given options the one expressing that idea is A — "End system by NIC".

Wording note: the option text appears garbled in the source paper ("End system by NIC"). Interpreting the intended meaning, the application layer lives in the end system; the NIC works at layers 1–2 and the Ethernet standard defines the lower layers, so B, C and D are wrong.
MCQ 59
Question

Application layer offers _______ service.

MCQUnit 33.2. Concepts of OSI Layers

Options:

  1. A. End to end
  2. B. Process to process
  3. C. Both a & b
  4. D. None of the mentioned

Correct Answer:

C — Both a & b

Explanation:

Application-layer protocols offer an end-to-end service between the two communicating programs, and the data is finally delivered to the correct process (through the underlying transport layer using port numbers), so the paper's expected answer is C — Both a & b.

Concept clarification: strictly speaking, "process-to-process" delivery is the transport layer's job and the application layer provides "end-to-end" services to the user programs; the composite option is the one marked correct in the standard key. Write both terms with this clarification to secure full marks.

3.3. Important Protocols / Data Packets / Datagram

MCQ 60
Question

Packets of data that is transported by IP is called

MCQUnit 33.3. Important Protocols / Data Packets / Datagram ★

Options:

  1. A. datagrams
  2. B. Frames
  3. C. Segments
  4. D. Encapsulate message

Correct Answer:

A — datagrams

Explanation:

Packets transported by IP are called datagrams — option A.

  • B. Frames are the data link layer PDU (Ethernet).
  • C. Segments are the transport layer PDU of TCP.
  • D. "Encapsulate message" is not a PDU name; the complete unit at the application layer is simply called a message.
MCQ 61
Question

UDP needs the ____ address to deliver the user datagram to the correct application program

MCQUnit 33.3. Important Protocols / Data Packets / Datagram

Options:

  1. A. Application
  2. B. Physical
  3. C. Port
  4. D. Internet

Correct Answer:

C — Port

Explanation:

UDP uses the port number in its header to deliver the user datagram to the correct application program on the destination host — option C.

The socket address = IP address + port number. Standard ports: DNS 53, DHCP 67/68, TFTP 69, SNMP 161. UDP's header contains source port, destination port, length and checksum — only 8 bytes.

MCQ 62
Question

Which of the following protocol is considered as unreliable and connection less protocol?

MCQUnit 33.3. Important Protocols / Data Packets / Datagram ★

Options:

  1. A. UDP
  2. B. TCP
  3. C. IP
  4. D. None of these

Correct Answer:

A — UDP

Explanation:

UDP is the unreliable, connectionless transport protocol: no handshake, no acknowledgement, no retransmission, no ordering — option A.

  • B. TCP is connection-oriented and reliable (three-way handshake, ACK, retransmission).
  • C. IP is connectionless but it is a network-layer protocol, not the transport protocol the question refers to; the standard "unreliable and connectionless" protocol name in this context is UDP.
  • D is wrong because UDP fits.
MCQ 63
Question

Which is not an application layer protocol?

MCQUnit 33.3. Important Protocols / Data Packets / Datagram ★★

Options:

  1. A. HTTP
  2. B. FTP
  3. C. SMTP
  4. D. TCP

Correct Answer:

D — TCP

Explanation:

TCP is a transport-layer protocol, so among the four it is the one that is not an application layer protocol — option D.

  • A. HTTP — Web access (application layer).
  • B. FTP — file transfer (application layer).
  • C. SMTP — e-mail sending (application layer).
MCQ 64
Question

Which protocol is used for transfer files between computers?

MCQUnit 33.3. Important Protocols / Data Packets / Datagram

Options:

  1. A. FTP
  2. B. SMTP
  3. C. HTTP
  4. D. IP

Correct Answer:

A — FTP

Explanation:

FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is the protocol used to transfer files between computers over a network — option A. It uses TCP, with port 21 for control and port 20 (active mode, or a random port in passive mode) for data.

  • B. SMTP sends e-mail; C. HTTP transfers Web resources; D. IP is the network-layer addressing/routing protocol. (Note that HTTP also transfers files, but FTP is the dedicated file-transfer protocol asked for here.)
MCQ 65
Question

FTP is built on architecture.

MCQUnit 33.3. Important Protocols / Data Packets / Datagram

Options:

  1. A. Client-Server
  2. B. P2P
  3. C. Data Centric
  4. D. Service Oriented

Correct Answer:

A — Client-Server

Explanation:

FTP follows the client–server architecture: a client program connects to an FTP server, authenticates, and then uploads or downloads files — option A.

  • B. P2P — FTP is centralised on a server, so it is not peer-to-peer.
  • C. Data centric and D. Service oriented are architectural styles of software systems, not FTP's architecture.
MCQ 66
Question

Telnet is a ______ based computer protocol.

MCQUnit 33.3. Important Protocols / Data Packets / Datagram

Options:

  1. A. Sound
  2. B. Image
  3. C. Text
  4. D. Animation

Correct Answer:

C — Text

Explanation:

Telnet is a text-based (character-oriented) protocol: it carries keyboard characters to the remote host and returns character output, using the Network Virtual Terminal (NVT) standard. Hence C.

It cannot carry sound, images or animation — it has no graphics capability at all. It uses TCP port 23 and sends everything in plain text, which is why SSH is preferred today.

MCQ 67
Question

______ allows you to connect and login to a remote computer.

MCQUnit 33.3. Important Protocols / Data Packets / Datagram ★

Options:

  1. A. Telnet
  2. B. FTP
  3. C. SMTP
  4. D. HTTP

Correct Answer:

A — Telnet

Explanation:

Telnet allows you to connect and log in to a remote computer and work on it through a text terminal — option A.

  • B. FTP transfers files but does not give an interactive login session.
  • C. SMTP sends mail; D. HTTP transfers Web pages.

Security caution for the exam: Telnet is insecure (plain-text password) — modern practice is SSH (port 22), which provides the same remote login with encryption.

MCQ 68
Question

ICMP is primarily used for

MCQUnit 33.3. Important Protocols / Data Packets / Datagram

Options:

  1. A. Error and diagnostic functions
  2. B. Addressing
  3. C. Forwarding
  4. D. Routing

Correct Answer:

A — Error and diagnostic functions

Explanation:

ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) is used primarily for error reporting and diagnostic functions — option A. Examples: destination unreachable, time exceeded (TTL expiry), echo request/reply used by the ping command, and traceroute diagnostics.

  • B. Addressing — done by IP/DHCP; C. Forwarding and D. Routing — done by IP and routing protocols (RIP, OSPF, BGP). ICMP reports problems but does not route.

3.3.2. Presentation Layer Protocols

MCQ 69
Question

What is the full form of SSL?

MCQUnit 33.3.2. Presentation Layer Protocols ★★

Options:

  1. A. simple secure layer
  2. B. secure simple layer
  3. C. secure socket layer
  4. D. simple socket layer

Correct Answer:

C — secure socket layer

Explanation:

SSL = Secure Socket Layer — the security protocol created by Netscape, later standardised as TLS (Transport Layer Security), which provides encryption, integrity and authentication for applications such as HTTPS, IMAPS and FTPS. Hence C.

Options A, B and D are wrong rearrangements of the words. Exam note: SSL 2.0/3.0 are deprecated; modern HTTPS uses TLS 1.2/1.3, so write "SSL/TLS".

3.3. Concepts of IP Address

MCQ 70
Question

What IP address class allocates 8 bits for the host identification part?

MCQUnit 33.3. Concepts of IP Address ★★

Options:

  1. A. Class A
  2. B. Class B
  3. C. Class C
  4. D. Class D

Correct Answer:

C — Class C

Explanation:

Class C gives 8 bits to the host part (format N.N.N.H — 24 network bits + 8 host bits), so option C is correct. That is why a Class C network has only 28 − 2 = 254 usable addresses.

  • Class A → 24 host bits (16.7 million hosts); Class B → 16 host bits (65,534 hosts); Class D → no host part at all (multicast).
MCQ 71
Question

Which of the following address belongs class A?

MCQUnit 33.3. Concepts of IP Address ★★

Options:

  1. A. 121.12.12.248
  2. B. 128.12.12.248
  3. C. 129.12.12.248
  4. D. 130.12.12.248

Correct Answer:

A — 121.12.12.248

Explanation:

Class A covers first-octet values 1–126 (0 and 127 are special). Among the options, 121.12.12.248 starts with 121, so it belongs to Class A — option A.

  • B (128.x), C (129.x) and D (130.x) all fall in the range 128–191, which is Class B.

Remember the boundaries: A 1–126, B 128–191, C 192–223, D 224–239, E 240–255.

MCQ 72
Question

Which of the following is correct regarding Class B Address of IP address

MCQUnit 33.3. Concepts of IP Address

Options:

  1. A. Network bit - 14, Host bit - 16
  2. B. Network bit - 16, Host bit - 14
  3. C. Network bit - 18, Host bit - 16
  4. D. Network bit - 12, Host bit - 14

Correct Answer:

A — Network bit - 14, Host bit - 16

Explanation:

In a Class B address the first two bits are fixed as "10"; the remaining 14 bits identify the network and the last 16 bits identify the host — so the expected answer is A — Network bit − 14, Host bit − 16.

Ambiguity note: if you count the two fixed leading bits along with the 14 network bits, you get "16 network bits and 16 host bits" — which is exactly what option B says (though option B's format writes it as "Network − 16, Host − 14"). As per the standard classful convention (fixed prefix bits excluded), the correct option is A. To be safe in a university exam, write both statements and show the working: 10nnnnnn.nnnnnnnn.hhhhhhhh.hhhhhhhh.

3.4. Difference between HTTP and HTTPS

MCQ 73
Question

Difference between HTTP and HTTPS.

MCQUnit 33.4. Difference between HTTP and HTTPS ★★★★

Answer:

Direct answer: HTTP is the plain-text Web protocol on port 80; HTTPS is HTTP protected by SSL/TLS on port 443, with encryption, integrity and server authentication provided by a digital certificate.

Difference between HTTP and HTTPS
PointHTTPHTTPS
Full formHyperText Transfer ProtocolHyperText Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTP over SSL/TLS)
PortTCP 80 (plain)TCP 443
SecurityNo encryption — data is plain textEncrypted with TLS; confidentiality, integrity, authentication
CertificateNot requiredX.509 digital certificate from a Certificate Authority is required
SpeedSlightly faster (no TLS handshake)Slightly slower on first connection; HTTP/2, HTTP/3 and session resumption largely remove the difference
URL prefixhttp://https:// (padlock icon in the browser)
Data safetyPasswords, card numbers and cookies can be read or modified in transit (MITM attack)Protected against eavesdropping, tampering and server impersonation
SEO / browser behaviourMarked "Not secure" by modern browsers on formsPreferred by search engines; required for geolocation, camera, service workers
Typical usePublic, non-sensitive information pagesLogin, banking, e-commerce, e-mail, APIs, all modern sites

Conclusion: HTTPS = HTTP + TLS. Since almost every site needs authentication and private data, HTTPS is now the default choice; HTTP is retained only for non-sensitive or internal documentation.

MCQ 74
Question

Differentiate HTTP vs HTTPS.

MCQUnit 33.4. Difference between HTTP and HTTPS ★★★

Answer:

Direct answer: the difference between HTTP and HTTPS lies in security: HTTPS is HTTP inside a TLS-encrypted, authenticated channel, so passwords and data cannot be read or changed in transit.

Difference between HTTP and HTTPS
PointHTTPHTTPS
Full formHyperText Transfer ProtocolHyperText Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTP over SSL/TLS)
PortTCP 80 (plain)TCP 443
SecurityNo encryption — data is plain textEncrypted with TLS; confidentiality, integrity, authentication
CertificateNot requiredX.509 digital certificate from a Certificate Authority is required
SpeedSlightly faster (no TLS handshake)Slightly slower on first connection; HTTP/2, HTTP/3 and session resumption largely remove the difference
URL prefixhttp://https:// (padlock icon in the browser)
Data safetyPasswords, card numbers and cookies can be read or modified in transit (MITM attack)Protected against eavesdropping, tampering and server impersonation
SEO / browser behaviourMarked "Not secure" by modern browsers on formsPreferred by search engines; required for geolocation, camera, service workers
Typical usePublic, non-sensitive information pagesLogin, banking, e-commerce, e-mail, APIs, all modern sites

Conclusion: HTTPS = HTTP + TLS. Since almost every site needs authentication and private data, HTTPS is now the default choice; HTTP is retained only for non-sensitive or internal documentation.

UNIT 4 — MAIL SERVICES

4.1. Application Layer Services

MCQ 75
Question

Electronic mail uses which Application layer protocol?

MCQUnit 44.1. Application Layer Services ★★★

Options:

  1. A. HTTP
  2. B. FTP
  3. C. SMTP
  4. D. TCP

Correct Answer:

C — SMTP

Explanation:

Electronic mail uses SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) to send and transfer messages — option C (TCP port 25, or 587 for authenticated submission).

  • A. HTTP transfers Web pages, B. FTP transfers files, D. TCP is the transport protocol that SMTP itself uses (the question asks for the application-layer protocol).
MCQ 76
Question

Which protocol is used for Electronic mail?

MCQUnit 44.1. Application Layer Services

Options:

  1. A. SMTP
  2. B. HTTP
  3. C. FTP
  4. D. SIP

Correct Answer:

A — SMTP

Explanation:

The protocol used for electronic mail is SMTP — option A (for sending/transferring); the receiving side later uses POP3 or IMAP to retrieve messages from the mailbox.

  • B. HTTP — Web; C. FTP — file transfer; D. SIP — signalling for VoIP calls, not for e-mail.
MCQ 77
Question

Which one of the following protocol delivers/stores mail to receiver server?

MCQUnit 44.1. Application Layer Services ★

Options:

  1. A. SMTP
  2. B. HTTP
  3. C. IMAP
  4. D. POP

Correct Answer:

A — SMTP

Explanation:

SMTP is the protocol that delivers mail from the sender's mail server to the receiver's mail server, where the message is stored in the mailbox for later retrieval — hence option A.

  • D. POP and C. IMAP do the opposite job: the user's client pulls mail from the server. B. HTTP is used only for the Web interface of mail services.
MCQ 78
Question

SMTP uses which of the following TCP port?

MCQUnit 44.1. Application Layer Services ★

Options:

  1. A. 22
  2. B. 23
  3. C. 25
  4. D. 21

Correct Answer:

C — 25

Explanation:

SMTP uses TCP port 25 — option C. (Port 587 is used for authenticated submission from mail clients and 465 for SMTPS.)

  • A. 22 — SSH; B. 23 — Telnet; D. 21 — FTP control connection.

Useful port table: FTP 20/21, SSH 22, Telnet 23, SMTP 25, DNS 53, HTTP 80, POP3 110, IMAP 143, HTTPS 443, POP3S 995, IMAPS 993.

MCQ 79
Question

Expansion of SMTP is

MCQUnit 44.1. Application Layer Services ★★

Options:

  1. A. Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
  2. B. Simple Message Transfer Protocol
  3. C. Simple Mail Transmission Protocol
  4. D. Simple Message Transmission Protocol

Correct Answer:

A — Simple Mail Transfer Protocol

Explanation:

SMTP = Simple Mail Transfer Protocol — option A. It is the standard TCP/IP protocol (RFC 5321) for sending and transferring e-mail between servers and from clients to servers.

Options B, C and D ("Message"/"Transmission" variants) are distractors: the words are Simple Mail Transfer Protocol — remember "Mail Transfer", not "Mail Transmission" and not "Message Transfer".

MCQ 80
Question

POP3 stands for:

MCQUnit 44.1. Application Layer Services ★

Options:

  1. A. Post Open Protocol version3
  2. B. Post Office Protocol version3
  3. C. Passive Office Protocol version3
  4. D. Post Office Protocol version3

Correct Answer:

B — Post Office Protocol version3

Explanation:

POP3 = Post Office Protocol version 3 (RFC 1939) — the protocol a mail client uses to download messages from the mailbox. Among the options, B gives this expansion correctly.

Source note: the printed paper shows "Post Office Protocol version3" in both options B and D — an obvious duplication/typographic slip in the question paper. Use option B (and quote the standard expansion Post Office Protocol version 3) in the exam; the other expansions ("Post Open", "Passive Office") are wrong.
MCQ 81
Question

DNS is the abbreviation of

MCQUnit 44.1. Application Layer Services ★★

Options:

  1. A. Dynamic Name System
  2. B. Dynamic Network System
  3. C. Domain Name System
  4. D. Domain Name Services

Correct Answer:

C — Domain Name System

Explanation:

DNS = Domain Name System — option C. It is the hierarchical, distributed naming service that translates domain names (www.gtu.ac.in) into IP addresses (14.139.4.10), using UDP/TCP port 53.

  • A. Dynamic Name System — DHCP is the "dynamic" configuration protocol, not DNS.
  • B. Dynamic Network System and D. Domain Name Services are wrong expansions (the correct expansion uses "System", singular).
MCQ 82
Question

DNS database contains

MCQUnit 44.1. Application Layer Services ★

Options:

  1. A. Name server records
  2. B. Hostname-to-address records
  3. C. Hostname aliases
  4. D. All of the mentioned

Correct Answer:

D — All of the mentioned

Explanation:

A DNS database (zone) can contain name-server records (NS), hostname-to-address records (A/AAAA) and hostname aliases (CNAME) — all of the mentioned — so option D is correct.

Other record types worth quoting: MX (mail exchanger), PTR (reverse lookup), SOA (start of authority), TXT/SPF (e-mail authentication).

4.1.3. URL and URL Types

MCQ 83
Question

The location of a resource on the internet is given by its?

MCQUnit 44.1.3. URL and URL Types ★

Options:

  1. A. Protocol
  2. B. URL
  3. C. E-mail address
  4. D. ICQ

Correct Answer:

B — URL

Explanation:

The location of a resource on the Internet is given by its URL (Uniform Resource Locator) — option B, e.g. https://www.gtu.ac.in/index.html.

  • A. Protocol tells how to access the resource, not where it is.
  • C. E-mail address identifies a mailbox; D. ICQ is an old instant-messaging service.
MCQ 84
Question

In the network HTTP resources are located by

MCQUnit 44.1.3. URL and URL Types ★★

Options:

  1. A. Uniform resource identifier
  2. B. Unique resource locator
  3. C. Unique resource identifier
  4. D. Union resource locator

Correct Answer:

A — Uniform resource identifier

Explanation:

HTTP resources are located by a URI (Uniform Resource Identifier); among the options the correctly written standard term is A.

Ambiguity note: a URL (Uniform Resource Locator) — option B says "Unique resource locator" — is the type of URI that gives an HTTP resource's location. Since the paper misspells "Unique" instead of "Uniform", the standard answer key accepts option A. Both A and B would be true in a corrected version; in this bank option A is the safe answer and you should mention that a URL is a kind of URI.
MCQ 85
Question

The first line of HTTP request message is called:

MCQUnit 44.1.3. URL and URL Types ★

Options:

  1. A. Request line
  2. B. Header line
  3. C. Status line
  4. D. Entity line

Correct Answer:

A — Request line

Explanation:

The first line of an HTTP request message is the request line, which contains the method, the resource URL and the HTTP version — e.g. GET /index.html HTTP/1.1. Hence option A.

  • B. Header line — the following lines that carry Host, User-Agent, Accept, Cookie, etc.
  • C. Status line — the first line of the response (e.g. HTTP/1.1 200 OK).
  • D. Entity line — not a standard term; the body part is called the entity body.

4.2. Case Study of Email

MCQ 86
Question

Which of the following is an example of user agents for e-mail?

MCQUnit 44.2. Case Study of Email ★

Options:

  1. A. Microsoft Outlook
  2. B. Facebook
  3. C. Google
  4. D. Tumblr

Correct Answer:

A — Microsoft Outlook

Explanation:

Microsoft Outlook is a mail user agent (MUA) — the client software used to compose, send and read e-mail — so option A.

  • Facebook, Google and Tumblr are websites/social services; although Gmail is an e-mail service, "Google" as such is a search/technology company, not a mail user agent program.

Other examples of MUAs: Mozilla Thunderbird, Apple Mail, Outlook Web App, K-9 Mail.

4.3. Case Study of Locating Website / Search Engine

MCQ 87
Question

What is search Engine? Explain the process of locating website.

MCQUnit 44.3. Case Study of Locating Website / Search Engine ★★★

Answer:

Direct answer: a search engine crawls the Web into an index and answers queries with a ranked list of results; locating a website means opening a result link, after which DNS, TCP, TLS and HTTP fetch and display the page.

Definition: A search engine is a Web-based software system that helps users find information on the World Wide Web. The user types keywords or a question (a query); the search engine matches the query against its own pre-built index of Web pages and returns a ranked list of results with the page title, URL and a short snippet. Popular examples: Google, Bing, Yahoo, DuckDuckGo, Baidu, Yandex.

Components of a search engine
ComponentFunction
Crawler / spider / robot (e.g. Googlebot)Automatically visits pages starting from seed URLs and sitemaps, follows the links found on each page and brings back the page content; respects robots.txt.
Indexer / indexer-databaseParses the fetched pages, removes formatting, extracts words, links, images and metadata, and stores them in an inverted index (word → list of documents).
Query processor / search algorithmParses the user's query, expands synonyms, finds matching documents in the index and ranks them.
Ranking algorithmOrders results by relevance: keyword match and location, page authority (PageRank-style link analysis), freshness, HTTPS, mobile-friendliness, page speed, user engagement.
User interfaceThe search box and the results page, plus filters (images, videos, news, maps, time range) and ads.
Process of locating a website with a search engine (step by step)
  1. User enters a query in the search box, e.g. "GTU network technology syllabus".
  2. Query processing: the engine tokenises the words, corrects spelling, removes stop words, expands synonyms and may use the user's location/language.
  3. Index lookup: the inverted index is searched for the query terms; the engine gets the list of candidate documents containing them (this is why the reply is almost instant — the Web is not searched live).
  4. Ranking: candidates are scored with hundreds of signals — term frequency and position, anchor text, number and quality of inbound links, page freshness, site trust, HTTPS, load speed, and personalisation.
  5. Result page (SERP): the ranked list is formatted with title, URL, snippet and rich results (images, reviews, maps, "People also ask"); the best answer may appear in a featured snippet or knowledge panel.
  6. User clicks a result → the browser accesses that URL: DNS resolution → TCP connection → TLS (if https) → HTTP GET → the Web server returns the page → the browser renders it. This is the same URL-access case study described in the previous section.
  7. Feedback: the engine records the click (CTR), dwell time and pogo-sticking, and later uses fresh crawls of the site to update the index — this is the basis of SEO (Search Engine Optimisation).
Search operators, advantages and limitations
  • Handy operators: "exact phrase", site:gtu.ac.in, filetype:pdf, intitle:topology, -unwanted, OR.
  • Advantages: finds relevant pages among billions, instant results, free, works in every language, adds maps, images, news, videos, shopping, and can answer direct questions.
  • Limitations: results depend on the algorithm and can be manipulated by SEO spam; not all pages are indexed (deep Web, login-protected pages); privacy issues (queries are logged/profiled); ads compete with the real results; a crawler may show outdated content; SEO-friendly wording is needed for a site to be found.
  • How to get a website listed: publish it on a public server with a domain name, allow crawlers in robots.txt, submit the sitemap/URL to the search engine, link it from other sites, and keep the content unique and well-structured (titles, headings, meta description, HTTPS).

Conclusion: a search engine crawls the Web into an index and answers queries with a ranked result list; locating a website means opening a result, after which DNS resolution, the TCP connection, the TLS handshake and the HTTP request fetch and display the page.

MCQ 90
Question

A ______ is the physical path over which a message travels.

MCQUnit 44.3. Case Study of Locating Website / Search Engine

Options:

  1. A. Path
  2. B. Medium
  3. C. Protocol
  4. D. Route

Correct Answer:

B — Medium

Explanation:

The physical path over which a message travels is the medium (transmission medium: twisted pair, coaxial, fibre, radio) — option B.

  • A. Path is the logical route taken through the network (sequence of routers).
  • C. Protocol is the set of communication rules.
  • D. Route is the path selected by routing protocols — a logical concept, not a physical path.

SECTION 2 — SHORT QUESTIONS (62 questions)

UNIT 1 — INTRODUCTION TO NETWORK

Short 1
Question

What is Network? Explain advantages and disadvantages of Networks.

ShortUnit 11.1. Basics of Network ★★★

Answer:

Definition / direct answer: a network is a set of interconnected autonomous computers that share data and resources; it offers many advantages but also brings cost and security concerns.

Definition / direct answer: A computer network is a collection of two or more autonomous computers (and other devices such as printers, switches and servers) interconnected by a transmission medium — guided (cable) or unguided (wireless) — and following a common set of rules called protocols, so that they can exchange data and share hardware, software and information resources.

Each device in the network (called a node or host) can both send and receive data; no node is the master of another node — this is why the term autonomous is used in the definition. Data travels over the network in small units such as frames, packets and segments.

Advantages of networking
AdvantageExplanation
Resource sharingOne printer, scanner, plotter or disk array can be used by all users, saving money and space.
File and data sharingFiles can be copied and accessed across machines quickly instead of using pen drives or e-mail.
CommunicationE-mail, chat, video conferencing, VoIP and social applications depend completely on networks.
Centralised managementSoftware installation, user accounts, antivirus updates and policies are managed from a server for all clients.
Easier backup and reliabilityData is stored on servers with RAID and scheduled backups; a failed PC does not destroy the data.
Cost effectivenessShared Internet connection, shared licensed software and distributed processing reduce per-user cost.
Scalability and remote accessNew nodes and new sites can be added easily; users can work from home or branch offices (VPN, cloud).
Disadvantages of networking
DisadvantageExplanation
High initial costCabling, switches, servers, licences and skilled manpower are required.
Security threatsViruses, worms, ransomware, hacking, phishing and data leakage become possible.
Administration and maintenanceA network administrator, monitoring tools and periodic maintenance are essential.
Single point of failureIf the server or central switch fails, the whole network (or a large part of it) may stop working.
Performance dependenceSpeed falls when traffic increases; congestion, collisions and latency degrade service.
Privacy concernsEmployee activity can be monitored; personal data moves over shared media and may be intercepted.
Virus propagationMalware spreads from one machine to many in seconds.
Conclusion: Networking multiplies the usefulness of a computer many times over by sharing resources and enabling communication; the cost is money, administration effort and security risk, which are controlled by proper design, firewalls, antivirus and trained staff.

Conclusion: a network links two or more autonomous computers so that they can exchange data and share hardware, software and information resources; its advantages — resource and file sharing, communication, centralised management, easier backup, lower cost and scalability — are weighed against its disadvantages — high initial cost, security threats, administration effort, a single point of failure and performance dependence — which are reduced by careful design, firewalls, antivirus software and trained staff.

Short 2
Question

What is networking? Explain advantages, disadvantages and need of network.

ShortUnit 11.1. Basics of Network ★

Answer:

Definition / direct answer: Networking is the process/technology of interconnecting two or more autonomous computers and devices with a transmission medium and common protocols so that they can communicate and share resources. The resulting arrangement is called a computer network.

Definition / direct answer: A computer network is a collection of two or more autonomous computers (and other devices such as printers, switches and servers) interconnected by a transmission medium — guided (cable) or unguided (wireless) — and following a common set of rules called protocols, so that they can exchange data and share hardware, software and information resources.

Each device in the network (called a node or host) can both send and receive data; no node is the master of another node — this is why the term autonomous is used in the definition. Data travels over the network in small units such as frames, packets and segments.

Advantages of networking
AdvantageExplanation

Disadvantages of networking
DisadvantageExplanation
